description: 🚀 HACKNOVA is a team of passionate students focused on AI/ML, Full-Stack Development, Data Science, UI/UX, and Space Technology. We love hackathons, innovation, and building real-world solutions using technology and NASA data. 🌎🛰️
summary:
Field Shift turns NASA satellites into a personal climate shield for farmers, translating complex orbital telemetry into adaptive, multi-year crop rotation schedules.

By fusing observation streams from NASA SMAP (root moisture), GPM (precipitation radar), Landsat 8/9 (canopy health), ECOSTRESS (thermal crop stress), and GRACE-FO (groundwater storage) with USDA soil records, the platform eliminates guesswork. Instead of deciphering raw spectral indices, growers receive intuitive, plain-language recommendations tailored to their fields, complete with interactive priority controls and real-time drought stress simulators.

This shift is critical because decades of monoculture farming have drained aquifers and exhausted natural soil fertility. Field Shift empowers farmers to transition toward resilient legume and cereal rotations that cut irrigation demand by 52%, restore over 60 kg/ha of natural biological nitrogen, and protect farm revenue against extreme heat and drought. By bridging space science and farm reality, Field Shift safeguards planetary food security from the soil up.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Field Shift is an AI-powered agricultural decision-support web platform that transforms NASA Earth observations into actionable, climate-resilient crop rotation schedules.

Farmers select or draw their field parcel on an interactive map. Field Shift immediately queries and fuses five core NASA satellite missions alongside USDA soil records:

  1. NASA SMAP (L-band 1.4 GHz): Measures root-zone soil moisture (0–50 cm0\text{--}50\text{ cm}0–50 cm) to detect subterranean water deficits.
  2. NASA GPM / IMERG: Tracks 30-day radar precipitation accumulation against 20-year climatological baselines.
  3. Landsat 8/9 & Sentinel-2: Analyzes high-resolution (30m) NDVI to monitor vegetative canopy health and vigor.
  4. NASA ECOSTRESS: Captures thermal infrared land surface temperatures and evaporative stress on the crop canopy.
  5. NASA GRACE-FO: Detects regional terrestrial water storage anomalies to warn against unsustainable groundwater pumping.

Our multi-objective optimization engine (Score=∑wi⋅Si\text{Score} = \sum w_i \cdot S_iScore=∑wi​⋅Si​) calculates the optimal sequence of crops over a 3-year timeline, balancing water conservation, soil nitrogen replenishment, economic profitability, and climate resilience. Farmers can interactively adjust priority sliders and use our "What-If" Climate Stress Simulator to virtually test how their crop rotations hold up against severe droughts (−35%-35\%−35% rain, +3.5∘C+3.5^\circ\text{C}+3.5∘C temperature spikes) before sowing a single seed.

What Benefits It Has

  • Translates Space Telemetry into Farmer Action: Replaces intimidating raw scientific indices (e.g., NDVI 0.589 or SMAP 42%) with clear, plain-language advisories (e.g., "Canopy Vigour: Good", "Root-Zone Moisture: Adequate").
  • Significant Water Savings: Replaces water-intensive monocultures with drought-hardy pulses and millets, achieving 52% irrigation water savings.
  • Biological Soil Regeneration: Strategic legume integration naturally fixes +55 to +60 kg/ha+55\text{ to }+60\text{ kg/ha}+55 to +60 kg/ha of organic nitrogen, drastically cutting expensive synthetic fertilizer costs.
  • Audit-Ready Reporting: Features a one-click Executive Farm Advisory Report Generator with clean print-to-PDF formatting for bank loans, insurance compliance, and agricultural extension advisors.

Intended Impact

Monoculture farming and accelerating climate volatility are depleting global aquifers and degrading topsoil fertility. Field Shift empowers smallholder and commercial growers to transition from high-risk monocropping to adaptive, regenerative rotations. By providing a mathematical buffer against extreme heat and drought, Field Shift stabilizes farm incomes, prevents catastrophic crop failures, and builds planetary food security from the soil up.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software

  • Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Lucide React, Recharts (interactive telemetry time-series and multi-criteria comparison bar charts), Leaflet.js (GIS farm parcel mapping).
  • Backend: Python 3.11, Django, Django REST Framework, Scikit-learn, NumPy, Pandas, Gunicorn, WhiteNoise.
  • Cloud & Authentication: Supabase Cloud Authentication with live JWT token exchange and role-based access control.
  • Earth Observation & Agronomic Data: NASA Earthdata APIs, NASA POWER agroclimatology, MODIS/VIIRS, OpenET ensemble evapotranspiration, and USDA SSURGO soil survey databases (26 total cataloged datasets).
  • Deployment: Production-configured for Render via automated render.yaml blueprint with active GitHub CI/CD integration.

How It Is Creative & Innovative

Most satellite agriculture tools simply display colorful heatmaps, leaving growers to guess what to do next. Field Shift is creative because it acts as an Action Engine, not just an observation dashboard.

  • It uniquely couples satellite telemetry directly to a predictive crop sequence algorithm.
  • It features an interactive Climate Stress "What-If" Lab, allowing farmers to simulate worst-case climate shocks and see their resilience score dynamically adjust.
  • It respects real-world farmer autonomy through customizable priority weightings—letting farmers prioritize between water conservation, soil health, or immediate cash margin.

Factors Our Team Considered

  1. Outdoor Usability: Outdoor-readable color palettes, minimum 44px touch targets, high contrast, and responsive layout for tractor-cab or smartphone usage.
  2. Agronomic Science Rules: Enforcing rotational safety (prohibiting back-to-back same-family nightshades to prevent pest buildup, respecting root-depth layering to break subsoil compaction).
  3. Data Transparency & Provenance: Every metric displays its exact satellite sensor, spatial resolution, and temporal cadence so agricultural advisors can trust the data.
  4. Zero-Friction Access: Pre-configured one-click verified demo profiles (Sarah Jenkins, Farm Producer and Dr. Marcus Vance, NASA Science Advisor) allow reviewers and judges to evaluate live production features instantly without setup barriers.
